title: Develop service/solution and integration strategy
goal: Every capability the venture needs has one written answer of build, buy or connect, the standards the venture's own code follows are written down, and the components it reuses are listed with the terms they come under.

steps.do: List the capabilities the product needs, and for each one write whether the venture should build it, buy it or connect an existing system, with the evidence behind the answer (what the capability is worth to the customer, what it would cost to run, and whether it is the venture's own advantage), leaving the choice itself to the founder where money or a dependency is involved.

Write the standards the venture's own code follows: the languages and versions, where code lives, how a change is reviewed and tested, how secrets are kept out of the repository, and what has to be true before anything reaches a customer, and keep it to rules the venture can actually hold to at its size.

Score the candidate development tools and services against the venture's own criteria with the tool-selection skill, favouring the one that gives the venture a record of its own work, and record each tool the venture adopts as a connection with its scopes and what it is authoritative for.

Write the test a component has to pass before the venture depends on it: a licence the venture can live with, a maintainer still shipping, a way out, no secret sent to a third party, and a size the venture can read, and say which of these are absolute.

For each capability marked buy or connect, name the candidate components, run each one against the criteria, record the licence and the terms it comes under, and bring any component whose terms the venture must accept, or that costs money, to the founder.

Keep one list of every component the venture depends on, with its version, its licence, who maintains it, when it was last updated and which part of the product would stop without it, and mark the ones that are no longer maintained.

consider.why: A dependency list nobody keeps is how an unmaintained component stays in a product for years.
consider.when: The venture ships code of its own, or depends on more than a handful of components.

steps.do: Write how an exception to these standards is asked for and recorded: who may grant it, for how long, what evidence it needs, and what has to happen before it expires, and record each exception already in force.

consider.why: Without a way to record an exception, a standard is either broken quietly or blocks the work.
consider.when: More than one person or agent role writes the venture's code, or a standard has already been broken once.

steps.do: Add each build, buy or connect answer as evidence to the decision it bears on, and raise to the product lead the order in which the capabilities should be built or connected.

done_criteria.check: Does every capability the product needs carry one answer of build, buy or connect with its evidence, and is every component the venture would depend on checked against the criteria with its licence recorded?
